newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends firmer in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends firmer in quiet trading.

text.p: The Canadian dollar ended firmer at C$1.3892 (US$0.7198) on Monday from Friday's close of C$1.3918 (US$0.7184) in quiet trade, dealers said.
They said Canada dollar buying on the International Monetary Market in Chicago boosted the unit ahead of U.S. retail sales data out on Tuesday.

Analysts said April retail sales are expected to provide evidence of inflationary pressure in the U.S. economy and heighten or decrease expectations of a possible hike in interest rates when the Federal Open Market Committee meets on May 20.

A Reuter survey of economists forecast that U.S. retail sales for April were down 0.3 percent, compared to 0.1 percent rise in the previous month. A lower than expected number of retail sales could lessen expectations of a U.S. rate rise.
Traders said some investors were holding tight to their current positions ahead of tonight's election debate among the leaders of the five major parties contesting the Canadian election on June 2.
Analysts have said the debate could hurt the ruling Liberals and may boost the fortunes of one or more of the opposition parties.
Interest rate speculation could heat up this week as the United States releases a slew of data, including retail sales, producer prices and the consumer price index.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 85.86 yen from Friday's close of 86.27 and rose to 1.2284 marks from Friday's 1.2111 marks.
